assertion: The Twin Cities recorded its second-warmest September and October in 2026, averaging 62.4 degrees.
measure: Minneapolis monthly average temperature GHCN daily

assertion: Only 2024 was warmer, with an average temperature of 63.8 degrees during the two-month period.
sql: SELECT AVG((tmax_c+tmin_c)/2)*9/5+32 FROM weather.ghcnd_daily WHERE station_id='USW00014922' AND SUBSTR(CAST("date" AS VARCHAR),1,4)='2024' AND SUBSTR(CAST("date" AS VARCHAR),6,2) IN ('09','10')

assertion: Five of the past six years rank among the 10 warmest combined Septembers and Octobers in the Twin Cities.
Additionally, 2021, 2023 and 2025 also rank among the top 10 warmest.
September and October temperatures in the Twin Cities have been warming for at least the past two decades.
inaccuracy: Year-to-year noise is large (2020 was 52.3 F); trend is clear only in multi-year averages
independent_value: 1991-2005 mean about 55.7 F vs 2006-2026 about 58.2 F

assertion: Warmer falls may feel normal to Minnesotans.
reason: A perception claim about how people feel; no data can test it.
